museum_text.zh: 范寬向來被視為山水成立期的大師，可惜生平不詳，只知他曾隱居終南、太華，晚年來往於開封、洛陽間，但未入朝任職，大約一○二五年時還在世。本幅被公認為他的真蹟，甚至視為宋代山水畫的代表形象。 畫中山水並非模仿真實空間為目標，而是巧妙地在近、中、遠三段式的基本構圖中，藉推遠主山、拉近中景、突顯近景渺小行旅與主山巍峨崇高的對比等手法，創造了一種如臨其境的壯碩山水之趣。 畫幅右下角樹蔭中藏有「范寬」二字款，左下腳則有「忠孝之家」印，為錢勰所有，他也是蘇軾的朋友。
museum_text.en: Fan K'uan has long been considered a founding master of Chinese landscape painting. Unfortunately, little is known about him, including his birth and death dates. However, he apparently lived in reclusion in the Chung-nan and T'ai-hua Mountains, and in later years traveled between K'ai-feng and Loyang. He never became an official and was still living around 1025. This is universally regarded as an authentic work of his and representative of Sung landscape painting, especially the Northern Sung monumental manner. The artist's purpose here apparently was not to replicate realistic space. Rather, by cleverly manipulating the basic compositional blocks of the fore-, middle-, and background, he could push back the main mountain peak, reign in the middleground, and focus on the minute travelers in the foreground. With the dramatic contrast between tiny figures and towering central mountains, the artist created an interesting scene placing the viewer in the midst of a monumental landscape. In the lower right corner, hidden among the trees, is the brief signature “Fan K’uan”, and in the lower left is the seal “Chung-hsiao chih chia” (Of the Family of Chung-hsiao). The latter belonged to Ch'ien Hsieh, a friend of the Northern Sung literary great Su Shih.

intro.zh: 一座高耸的主峰占满了这幅绢本立轴的大半，中段是雾气和流水。
intro.en: A towering central peak fills most of this tall silk scroll, with mist and water across the middle.

intro.zh: 山脚的路上有一队骡马，几乎小得看不见。
intro.en: At its foot a mule train is barely visible on the road, tiny beside the cliffs.

intro.zh: 范宽曾隐居终南、太华山中，约1025年时仍在世；馆方说，此画被公认为他的真迹，也是北宋雄伟山水的代表。
intro.en: Fan Kuan lived as a recluse in the Zhongnan and Taihua mountains and was still alive around 1025; the museum calls this painting universally accepted as his genuine work and representative of Northern Song monumental landscape.

intro.zh: 馆方解释，画家并不模仿真实空间，而是把主峰推远、突出近景渺小的行旅，让观者仿佛置身于雄伟的山水之中。
intro.en: The museum explains that he did not set out to copy real space: he pushed the main peak back and focused on the minute travellers, so that the viewer feels placed inside a monumental landscape.

look_for.zh: 右下方的骡马队，在岩石旁显得极小。
look_for.en: The mule train at the lower right, tiny beside the rocks.

look_for.zh: 右侧山崖上细细垂下的一道瀑布。
look_for.en: The thin waterfall dropping down the cliff on the right.

look_for.zh: 右下角树丛中藏着的“范宽”二字款，直到1958年才被重新发现。
look_for.en: The signature 范寬 (Fan Kuan), hidden among the trees in the lower right corner, rediscovered only in 1958.

look_for.zh: 馆方记录把山石的画法列为“雨点皴”：由无数短促的笔点堆成。
look_for.en: The museum's record lists the rock texture as 'raindrop' texture strokes (雨點皴), built up from countless short dabs.

alt.zh: 一幅高大的立轴：一座巨大而深暗的山崖，右侧有瀑布，山下是一道雾气，近景是树木和一条小路。
alt.en: A tall hanging scroll: a huge, dark cliff face with a waterfall on its right, a band of mist below, and trees and a small path in the foreground.

views.zh: 他在画上方的诗塘题字，认定这是北宋范宽（字中立）的作品。
views.en: On the poem panel above the painting he identified it as a work by Fan Kuan (style name Zhongli) of the Northern Song.

quote.zh: 北宋范中立谿山行旅圖。董其昌觀。

about.zh: 艺术史学者，《中国艺术》作者
about.en: art historian, author of The Arts of China

views.zh: 维基百科引用他的论述：这幅画为雄伟山水画树立了一种理想。
views.en: Wikipedia, citing his account, says the painting establishes an ideal in monumental landscape painting.

note.zh: 每一句都对照所注出处核对过；找不到可靠出处的说法已删去或改写。
note.en: Every sentence was checked against the sources it cites; claims without a reliable source were cut or rewritten.
